name: Verify vendor bank detail changes with Google Sheets, email and Telegram

parameters.content:
GUARDRAIL - vendor bank-detail change guard

Who it's for: finance and accounts-payable teams that receive vendor payment-detail changes by email.

How it works: every request is held in a pending state. The IBAN is validated (format, mod-97 checksum and country match), the vendor is matched against your sheet and the request is scored for risk. A single-use approval link goes only to the finance address already on file, never to the sender. Approval is refused until the cooling period ends (48 h, or 72 h for higher risk); replays, unknown and expired links are denied and logged. A daily watchdog reminds at 24 h, escalates at 48 h and closes the request as expired at 72 h, with one digest instead of per-vendor noise. Every attempt lands in an append-only audit tab.

How to set up: create the Vendors, BankChanges and Audit tabs (headers in the Setup note), set base_url and finance_lead in the three Config nodes, connect the Google Sheets, SMTP and Telegram credentials, then activate.

Requirements: Google Sheets, an SMTP account, a Telegram bot and a public n8n URL. No paid services.

How to customize: change thresholds, cooling periods and token TTL in the Config nodes; add or remove form fields in the trigger.

SETUP CHECKLIST (10 minutes)

1. Create one Google Sheet with three tabs and these exact headers:
   Vendors: vendor_code | vendor_name | country | vendor_domain | finance_email | finance_lead_email | status
   BankChanges: change_id | vendor_code | vendor_name | requested_by | finance_email | finance_lead_email |
     new_iban | new_iban_masked | iban_hash | bank_country | risk | risk_flags | status | token_hash |
     created_at | cooling_until | expires_at | last_stage | last_action_at | decided_by | note
   Audit: at | event | change_id | actor | detail
2. Fill Vendors with the finance address you trust TODAY (not the one in the request).
3. Open Config (intake), Config (approval) and Config (watchdog) and set base_url,
   company and finance_lead. Keep the three copies identical.
4. Connect Google Sheets, SMTP and Telegram credentials on the red nodes.
5. Activate. The form lives at /form/vendor-bank-change.

The sheet can be the source of truth: a human can read it, and status is the state machine.
Restrict access: it holds bank details (treat it as confidential data).

PART A - intake

Validate first (IBAN mod-97, country match, requester email), then match the vendor and
score risk. Nothing is emailed to the request address: the verification link goes only to
the finance contact already on file.

Risk rules (sum, capped at 100): unknown vendor 100 | inactive 40 | bank country vs IBAN 30 |
requester domain 25 | free mailbox 15 | second change in 90 days 15 | 2+ changes 30.
>= 70 goes to manual review. 40+ uses the long cooling period.

PART B - one-click decision

The link carries a random token. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored, so a leaked sheet
cannot be used to approve anything. Each token works once: a second click returns
"Already handled" and changes nothing (idempotent).

Approve before the cooling period ends is refused and the state is untouched.
Expired or unknown tokens are logged in Audit as LINK_DENIED with HTTP 400.

PART C - watchdog

Runs daily at 07:30. Stage 1 (24 h) reminds finance, stage 2 (48 h) escalates to the
finance lead, stage 3 (72 h) closes the hold as EXPIRED and tells the requester.
last_stage in the sheet guarantees a stage is never sent twice.

Links are never re-sent - the email says to use the original one. That is deliberate:
re-sending a link turns a reminder into a second attack surface.

AUDIT

Append-only rows for anything refused or escalated: rejected submissions, duplicate
requests, manual reviews and denied links. Approved and rejected decisions also stamp
decided_by and last_action_at on the change row.
